Reflection & Self-Correction

Agents that critique their own outputs to improve quality, inspired by human iterative refinement.

Reflexion Framework

Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) uses verbal reinforcement to help agents learn from mistakes without weight updates. It consists of three models:

  1. Actor: Generates text/actions.
  2. Evaluator: Scores the output (Success/Failure).
  3. Self-Reflection: Verbalizes why it failed and stores this in episodic memory.

Self-RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)

A specific application of reflection where the model critiques its own retrieved documents and generated answers. It uses special "reflection tokens" to tag content as `[Relevant]`, `[Supported]`, or `[Useful]`.

Loop Recovery

A critical use of reflection is breaking out of loops. If an agent tries the same failed tool call 3 times, a standardized reflection step ("Why is this failing?") can trigger a strategy switch (e.g., "I should try a different search query").
